newsitem.title: FRANCE: French evacuate 1,778 people from Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: French evacuate 1,778 people from Brazzaville.

text.p: France's armed forces have evacuated 1,778 foreigners, two-thirds of them French nationals, from embattled Brazzaville in the Congo to nearby Gabon by air since Monday, a military spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine told reporters: "We are doing what we can. The military is doing everything they can. Our priority is to re-group and repatriate all those who want to leave in the best possible conditions."

Several dozen shocked evacuees arrived in Paris early on Wednesday and spoke of "butchery" in the streets of Brazzaville where supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and those of former Marxist military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso are engaged in their seventh day of clashes.

Some evacuees said they initially barricaded themselves in their homes, but increasingly fell prey to roaming bands of armed looters, including some who were uniformed members of the government forces.
"In the end, we became afraid that after looting, they would start raping our wives and children so we decided to pull out," one man told French television.

On Tuesday, French armoured cars protected convoys of civilian vehicles driven by French, Lebanese and other expatriate volunteers as they moved to different parts of the city centre to check on or collect potential evacuees.
The military spokeswoman said she did not know the nationalities of non-French evacuees among the 1,778 people flown to Gabon.
The evacuees who arrived in Paris unanimously praised the army. "The Foreign Legion was fantastic, they rescued us right at our doorstep," one man told French television.

But several were bitterly critical of the French embassy in Brazzaville. "They were totally disorganised and less interested about our safety than in playing a role in Congolese politics," another man said.
The clashes began on June 5 after soldiers surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on militias and illegal arms ahead of a July 27 presidential election.
Lissouba won a 1992 presidential election after Sassou Nguesso, president from 1979, bowed to calls for multi-party politics.

France has sent 400 troops to reinforce the 450 already in Brazzaville, where they were dispatched in March in case foreigners needed to be evacuated from Kinshasa during the civil war that toppled Zaire's Mobutu Sese Seko.

French government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said on Wednesday that power-sharing between President Jacques Chirac and new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin had "worked especially well" in responding to the Brazzaville fighting.
